A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InfoPO study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original InfoPO evaluations, training curves, ablations and robustness analyses on UserGym, ColBench, tau2-Bench, Sokoban and WebShop.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds original action-quality and reward-hacking analyses in Appendices B.5–B.6.

M1.justification: Equations (2)–(6) and Algorithm 1 retain the same counterfactual reward, normalization, variance gate and policy objective. The added support discussion clarifies applicability; the new diagnostic labels are explicitly excluded from training.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same UserGym environments, ColBench backend programming tasks, tau2-Bench domains, Sokoban, WebShop and simulator-shift scenarios. The added diagnostics examine retained task coverage without introducing a new dataset or interaction scenario.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in the benchmark and generalization experiments are unchanged. The new reward-hacking analysis reuses the existing without-gate ablation. IGPO is newly discussed in related work but is not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendices B.5–B.6 introduce post-hoc protocols that stratify current and next actions by quality, inspect the highest-reward 10% of turns, and compare targeted versus generic questions after matching response lengths. Existing training settings, splits and benchmark evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, masking sensitivity and interaction dynamics, v2 directly investigates whether information gain distinguishes useful from meaningless transitions and whether the variance gate prevents generic-question reward hacking. Tables 6–7 and Figures 10–11 substantially expand validation of the central reward mechanism.

E5.justification: Appendix B.5 adds a significance assessment comparing rewards for good and meaningless current actions, reporting p = 1.4 × 10^-108 without identifying the test. Existing three-seed mean-and-standard-deviation curves, four-run tau2-Bench evaluation and masking significance tests are unchanged.

E6.justification: The original benchmark results remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial diagnostic findings. Table 6 reports mean rewards of 0.380 versus 0.017 for good versus meaningless current actions. Table 7 reports length-matched targeted-versus-generic reward gaps of 0.319 for InfoPO and -0.055 without gating, alongside new question-frequency and interaction-length results.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–2, their proofs and the method's mathematical derivations are unchanged. Appendix B.6 adds the mathematical definition of a new diagnostic, the length-matched information-gain gap, as the expected reward difference over matched targeted-clarification and generic-question pairs.

C1.justification: The abstract, three stated contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about dense counterfactual credit, information-theoretic grounding, performance and generalization, including the claimed 14%–16% improvement over GRPO-based methods. The new diagnostics support these contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 explicitly states that InfoPO requires some task-relevant continuations and cannot recover useful structure from entirely degenerate trajectories or uninformative feedback. The new analyses also strengthen the interpretation of the reward as task-relevant sensitivity and of gating as protection against generic-question reward hacking. The existing limitations paragraph is retained.

D1.justification: Appendices B.5–B.6 add operational criteria for classifying action quality and question types and clarify that these labels are used only for analysis. These provide reproduction information for the new diagnostics, although implementation details remain limited. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, simulator prompts and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work newly contrasts IGPO's answer-conditioned belief improvement with InfoPO's masked-feedback action sensitivity. The bibliography adds IGPO, two Kong et al. papers, AutoEnv and USM, and removes Zhao et al.'s preference-following paper. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 adds localized method clarification, diagnostic summaries, Appendices B.5–B.6 and an Impact Statement, with limited related-work editing. It also replaces the preprint footer with proceedings information. The retained prose and overall section organization undergo little rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds a substantial diagnostic display block: Tables 6–7 and multi-panel Figures 10–11 showing sensitivity distributions, threshold rates and action-quality transitions. Existing figures retain their content but move with the text; the earlier case-study and prompt Figures 10–18 become Figures 12–20.

improvement.justification: The action-quality analysis and length-controlled gate comparison provide more direct evidence against arbitrary-distribution-shift and verbosity explanations than v1's existing diagnostics. The explicit support requirement also clarifies a failure boundary. These additions strengthen the mechanism argument, although incomplete sampling, labeling and significance-test details limit their evidential strength. The improvement is therefore useful but bounded.
